PRECONDITION vs DELIVERABLE (artifact kind: impl-plan) — a plan PROPOSES changes; it has not run.
Verify only that its PRECONDITIONS hold against the live repo:
  • the anchor / insertion-point text each edit attaches to EXISTS (verbatim);
  • assumed-existing files, symbols, and signatures are present;
  • the described edits would apply and compose.

DELIVERABLE — they are EXPECTED to be absent from the current repo. NEVER report
their absence as a finding. Only a missing or changed ANCHOR / PRECONDITION —
something an edit needs in order to land — is a defect.
A false claim about EXISTING code, a wrong signature, a drifted line number, or an internal contradiction remains a real finding.
If you nonetheless surface an expected-absence finding (the "absent" symbol is a plan DELIVERABLE mapped by the coverage-vs-source lens to a plan task), set that finding's deliverableAbsence:true so the gate scores it as expected work, never a blocker.

# assert-packaging-in-diff.sh — WAR worker packaging-floor guard (spec §4.1).
#
# Sibling of assert-test-in-diff.sh. Catches the enumerated-COPY class of
# container-packaging blind spot: a task ADDS a file next to source files a
# Dockerfile COPYs one-by-one, but nothing adds the new file to the image —
# the unit gate is green (the file sits beside its siblings in the repo tree),
# the audit is clean, the merge lands, and only the *image* crash-loops at
# deploy (the field incident: `case_metadata.py` added beside `loader.py`,
# `FileNotFoundError: /app/case_metadata.py`).
#
# Usage: assert-packaging-in-diff.sh <integration-base> <task-branch> \
#          [--repo <git-dir>] [--advise-vacuous]
# (--repo is test-only: points git at a fixture repo; production invokes from
#  the task-worktree cwd, exactly like assert-test-in-diff.sh.)
# --advise-vacuous: when the run is structurally vacuous under the ratified
#  scope below (no Dockerfile, or a non-empty diff with zero Added/Renamed/
#  Copied paths), print ONE informational advisory line to stderr citing that
#  scope. Opt-in only (the engine appends it when a plan explicitly declares
#  requiresPackaging: true) — stdout and every exit code stay byte-identical
#  without the flag. An entirely empty diff stays silent even with the flag.
#
# Diff = `git diff --name-status <base>...<branch>` (three-dot symmetric diff).
# ADDED (`A`), RENAME-TARGET (`R`), and COPY-TARGET (`C`) paths only — deletions
# and pure modifications never flag (removing a file a Dockerfile still COPYs is
# a *build* failure the docker gate or CI catches, not a packaging-floor concern).

# SCOPE RATIFICATION (ADR 0017 addendum): Added/Renamed/Copied-only is the
# INTENDED scope, not an oversight — this floor exists to catch the enumerated-
# COPY drift where a *new* file is born beside COPY'd siblings but nobody adds it
# to the image. A Modified or Deleted packaging artifact that breaks the image
# (an edited/removed file a Dockerfile still enumerates) surfaces as a docker
# *build* failure — the opt-in docker gate / CI's concern, not this floor's. A
# purely-Modified diff therefore exits 0 by design. See the dated addendum in
# docs/adr/0017-packaging-floor-docker-gate-ratified-backstops.md.

## Checkpoint (between phases)
Post a phase report — *landed (task→issue#, SHA) · the rendered **handoff block** (tipSha · polish merged/discarded/skipped · absorbed (sha → finding titles) · follow-ups filed (issue + why-not-absorbable) · asks parked (question + fork + task/seat/sha — the strike-list ruling gate's input) · notes · End-state condition statuses · intentPresent) · **Unexecuted backstops** (mandatory line rendering `handoff.backstops[]` — every deferred validation this phase did not run: each `check · why deferred · runner`, `source: 'auto'` entries flagged as Setup-recorded, and an **AI-declared** entry rendering its marker so it is never shown as operator-ratified; literal `None`/`— none —` when the array is empty, and the "no backstop section (pre-ratified-backstop plan)" note when it is `null`) · learnings captured · escalations needing your decision (with options) · deferred/blocked · gate result + working pushed@SHA · next phase?* — and **wait for the user's go**. Under `--afk`: post + `PushNotification`, then proceed. **Hard escalations (audit-blocked, unresolvable conflict, plan-contradiction) always halt regardless of mode.** Promote any ADR-worthy deviation to a real `docs/adr/` entry.
- **Manifest stamp (telemetry, fail-open).** Before posting the phase report, complete the Run-manifest section's on-phase-return stamp (`endedAt`, dispatch counts, task terminal statuses, `land`, envelope aggregates); a skipped stamp is the "unfinalized phase record" friction row `/war-review` reports; fail-open discipline unchanged (a failed write logs one line and never blocks the advance).
- **Issue-lifecycle floor — gate the DAG advance (§4.1).** Before advancing the DAG past this phase, run `bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/war/assets/assert-issues-filed.sh assert <ledger.json> <phase-id>` (it runs `gh-preflight.sh` itself first, so an account flip cannot fake its exit). It confirms the ledger's `epic_issue` and every `tasks[].issue` exist on live `gh`, and — on a phase being **landed** — that the epic is `state:CLOSED` **and** carries `status:done`. **Route by exit code:** `0` ⇒ verified, advance; `1` ⇒ blocks the advance, surfacing the named route (`issues-missing` naming the missing/null issue, or `done-but-open`) — treat as an escalation to resolve before proceeding; `2` ⇒ a gh/network/ledger-parse **tooling error**, escalate as such, **never a silent pass** (exit 2 never collapses into 1). On a **landed** phase, close the epic via the floor's atomic mode — `bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/war/assets/assert-issues-filed.sh --close-epic <n> --sha <sha>` (one call does `+status:done` / `−status:in-progress` **and** `gh issue close --reason completed` with the landed-SHA comment) — **instead of** separate label/close commands, so `status:done` can never outlive an open epic.
- **Follow-up filing floor — gate the DAG advance (D4, #1331).** Before advancing the DAG past a handoff-emitting phase (`landed` / `held:escalation`), every `handoff.followUps[]` entry must carry a **non-null `issue`** — the Workflow's `file-followups` dispatch normally stamps them (**consolidation precedes filing**: the engine collapses duplicate rows into `seats[]`-corroborated candidates pre-dispatch and asserts the returned `clusters[]` manifest — canonical: `FOLLOWUP_FILING_RESULT` in `assets/workflow-template.js`); any null ⇒ file it **now**, in a gh-write of its own (this floor fires at the Checkpoint, after the per-phase gh-write batch has closed, so run `gh-preflight.sh` for this write), **under the same discipline** — one issue per root cause, an open `war-followup` match gets a **corroboration comment**, never a new issue — and stamp the number into the ledger's phase `handoff` record. **Never advance over a null `issue`.**
- **Ask ruling gate — the strike list, gate the DAG advance absolutely (#1550, ADR 0013 amendment).** When `handoff.asks[]` is non-empty, **one gate rules all parked asks in a single pass**: render the strike list — one row per ask, its `question` + `fork` (the decision needed and its two branches) + task/seat/sha provenance, plus, on a citation-matched row, its `citationPrefill` (the engine's matched standing row + match rationale + executed sha + recommended ruling, #1879): the operator confirms or overrules in one stroke — never auto-unparked past a present operator, and a confirm-via-prefill is recorded as a citation-informed ruling in the same telemetry channel as an `--afk` citation resolution (the aced record's citation stamp) — and put it to the operator with the phase report. The advance floor is **absolute**: never advance the DAG over an unruled ask — interactively this binds as a hard wait (the run does not proceed until every row carries a ruling; no severity, count, or staleness exception). **Ruled-ask execution (ADR 0013 amendment 2026-08-27):** a ruled ask whose fix is fully specified **executes in this run** — injected into the next phase's decompose as a small first-class task carrying the ruling and its `suggested_fix`, or, in the final phase, ONE bounded polish-style post-land dispatch at the working tip. **Ruled-ask filing parity** is now filing-on-non-execution: file an issue **only** on **cannot-execute** (no vehicle, cross-task, budget) or execution-failure (regression ⇒ revert), the ruling recorded in it either way — never silently, never as default litter; when filed, it files Lead-side in a gh-write of its own, executed after this gate's ruling (the per-phase gh-write batch has already closed, so run `gh-preflight.sh` for this write), under the same discipline as engine-filed follow-ups — one issue per root cause carrying an `## Evidence artifacts` section, dedup-checked first against the engine-filed `handoff.followUps[]` rows and open `war-followup` issues (a match gets a corroboration comment, never a duplicate) — and mint each ruling as an adjudication row (the third producer, Decompose step 5) in **standing-row format** (today's ruling is tomorrow's `--afk` citation source), recorded in the ledger and threaded to every subsequent phase. Unruled asks are **never filed** — the engine already excludes them from consolidation and the file-followups dispatch; the Lead never re-adds one. **`--afk` posture:** a parked ask matching a standing adjudication row resolves by citation (the matched row quoted as the ruling) and may carry an **actionable absorb** outcome executed through the re-entry vehicle, its record carrying the matched **row-id + match rationale**; the row must cover the finding's NAMED trade-off, ambiguity is no-match; a no-match **demotes to follow-up with the question preserved** in the issue body — visibly not loss-free, flagged in the phase report; the unmatched ask files as a `follow-up` with `demote:ask-unruled-afk` on the body prefix line, question preserved (D13); a suppression row is minted **only from an operator ruling, provenance-marked** — `--afk` never mints one.
- **Never-waive rule (§4.4 — Lead prose).** A validation that is in **none** of: the resolved gate, a deterministic floor (test / packaging / submodule), or the plan's backstop section (a plan-declared or Setup-auto-recorded deferred validation) **may not be waived in prose mid-run**. Do not narrate it away as "skipped" or "not applicable" in a phase report — **escalate to the operator** instead (interactively wait; under `--afk` this is a hard escalation, since only the operator can ratify a new waiver). This is the behavioral fix for the silent-prose-waiver failure the whole feature exists to prevent — a deferred validation is legitimate only once it is a ratified backstop, never as an ad-hoc mid-run sentence.
- **Fail-closed phase classification (§4.2 — apply on every phase notification, before any land/hold/advance decision).** On each phase Workflow notification, derive `landDecision` as follows:
  1. If `status !== "completed"` (the Workflow timed out, was killed, or returned a non-`completed` notification) → classify as `held:phase-incomplete`.
  2. Else if the result is missing, unparseable, or `landDecision` is not in the known set (`landed`, `held:escalation`, `held:nothing-merged`, `held:land-failed`, `held:phase-incomplete`, `held:workflow-error`, `held:submodule-pr`) → classify as `held:workflow-error`.
  3. Else → use `result.landDecision` as returned.
  Never skip this gate — a phase that failed to run must never silently advance the DAG.
- **Outcome handling (§4.3):** when the derived `landDecision` is any `held:*` hold — or a task returned `env-blocked`, a merge/land `gate_failed` arrives (with or without a `gate_failure_class`), or you complete a phase's land manually — read [references/resume-and-recovery.md](references/resume-and-recovery.md) (§ Checkpoint outcome handling) and follow the matching arm: terminal vs retryable holds, the `held:land-failed` root-cause recipes, the escalation-completion land, `env-blocked` evidence gating, `gate_failed` class routing, manual-land hygiene, the exactly-once learnings capture after a manual land, the Recovery-relaunch entry points, and the held-partial-phase recovery runbook.

## Finish
When all phases land, run `bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_shared/gh-preflight.sh "<overrides.ghUser>"` **before opening the PR** (the Finish-PR gh-write site), then open **one PR** working → landing, body summarizing phases landed, learnings, escalations resolved, and follow-up issues filed. The body carries a mandatory **"Unexecuted backstops"** line (§4.4) — the union of every phase's `handoff.backstops[]` (plan-declared plus Setup-auto-recorded deferred validations), each rendered `check · why deferred · runner`, `source: 'auto'` entries flagged, and any **AI-declared** entry rendering its marker (never surfaced as operator-ratified); literal `None` when no phase deferred anything. This is the final land-time surface for every validation the run consciously left un-run. Report the PR URL. **Closing handoff:** point the operator at **`/war-review`** as the post-run step — it reads this run's manifest (`.claude/war/runs/<runId>.json`), renders the telemetry + friction report, and offers one confirmed friction issue.
